title: Robot Swarm Maze Pathfinding Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D robot swarm pathfinding simulation using Three.js and GLTFLoader (from CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.163.0/). Load TWO GLB assets:

1. 'CesiumMan.glb' — used as the robot swarm agents (load once, then clone/instance 8 times). Scale each clone to 0.4. These are the navigating robots.
2. 'DiffuseTransmissionTeacup.glb' — used as maze obstacle blocks. Load once, clone 12 times, scale each to 1.5, and arrange them in a grid-like maze pattern on the XZ plane (Y=0). Space obstacles ~4 units apart in a semi-random but navigable maze layout spanning roughly -20 to +20 on X and Z.

SCENE SETUP:
- Renderer: antialias, shadowMap enabled, size 100vw x 100vh, background color #1a1a2e.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera(60, aspect, 0.1, 200), positioned at (0, 35, 35), lookAt(0,0,0).
- Lights: AmbientLight(0x404060, 0.6), DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.2) at (15,30,15) casting shadows, HemisphereLight(0x8888ff, 0x444422, 0.4).
- Ground plane: 50x50, MeshStandardMaterial color #2a2a4a, receiveShadow.

ROBOT SWARM BEHAVIOR:
- Each of the 8 robots starts at a random position on the left side (X between -18 and -14, Z random between -15 and 15).
- A shared goal target position starts at (18, 0, 0) (right side), shown as a glowing yellow sphere (radius 0.5, emissive).
- Implement A*-like grid-based pathfinding: discretize the XZ plane into a 1x1 unit grid. Mark cells occupied by obstacles as blocked. Each robot computes a path from its current grid cell to the goal cell. Robots follow their path waypoint by waypoint at a configurable speed (default 3 units/sec).
- Robots avoid each other using simple separation: if two robots are within 1.5 units, apply a repulsion force pushing them apart.
- Robots that reach within 1.0 unit of the goal are marked as 'arrived'.
- Play the CesiumMan walk animation (AnimationMixer) on each robot while it is moving. Stop animation when arrived.

USER INTERACTIONS:
1. CLICK on the ground plane (raycasting) to MOVE the goal target to the clicked position. All robots recompute paths.
2. KEYBOARD 'R' — Reset: all robots return to random left-side start positions, goal resets to (18,0,0), arrived count resets.
3. KEYBOARD 'P' — Pause/Resume: toggle simulation pause. Robots freeze in place, animations pause.
4. KEYBOARD '+' / '=' — Increase robot speed by 1 (max 10).
5. KEYBOARD '-' — Decrease robot speed by 1 (min 1).
6. KEYBOARD 'U' — Undo last goal move (restore previous goal position, robots recompute). Support up to 5 undo levels.
7. DOM BUTTON 'Add Obstacle' — Places a new teacup obstacle clone at a random unoccupied grid cell near the center, rebuilds the pathfinding grid, all robots recompute paths.
8. DOM BUTTON 'Remove Obstacle' — Removes the last added obstacle, rebuilds grid, robots recompute.

HUD / UI:
- Top-left overlay div showing: Robot Speed, Arrived Count (X/8), Total Obstacles, Simulation State (running/paused), Goal Position (x,z rounded to 1 decimal), Elapsed Time (seconds since start/unpause).
- Two styled buttons at top-right: 'Add Obstacle' and 'Remove Obstacle'.

STATE MANAGEMENT — Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
{
  sceneReady: bool,
  robotCount: number (always 8),
  obstacleCount: number (initial 12, changes with add/remove),
  arrivedCount: number (0-8),
  robotSpeed: number (default 3),
  paused: bool (default false),
  goalPosition: {x, z} (rounded to 1 decimal),
  goalMoveCount: number (how many times goal was moved by click),
  undoStackSize: number (0-5),
  robotPositions: [{x, z}, ...] (8 entries, rounded to 1 decimal),
  robotStates: ['moving'|'arrived', ...] (8 entries),
  averageDistanceToGoal: number (mean Euclidean dist of all robots to goal, rounded to 2 decimals),
  elapsedTime: number (seconds, rounded to 1 decimal),
  totalPathRecomputes: number (incremented each time ALL robots recompute paths),
  lastAddedObstaclePos: {x, z} or null,
  lastRemovedObstaclePos: {x, z} or null,
  animationsPlaying: number (count of robots with active walk animation)
}

ENSURE:
- All robot positions remain within bounds [-24, 24] on X and Z.
- No robot position is ever NaN.
- arrivedCount + number of 'moving' robots always equals 8.
- Pathfinding grid is rebuilt whenever obstacles change.
- Undo stack never exceeds 5 entries.
- Speed is always clamped [1, 10].
- elapsedTime only increments when not paused.
physics_constraints: Robots must stay within [-24,24] XZ bounds. Separation force prevents overlap (min 1.5 unit distance enforced softly). Speed clamped [1,10]. arrivedCount + movingCount === 8 invariant. Undo stack max 5. No NaN positions. Elapsed time frozen when paused.
